name: Encoded PowerShell command line
description: PowerShell started with an encoded command (-enc / -EncodedCommand / -ec), a common way to hide stager code.
query: any where event.code in ("1", "4688") and process.name : "powershell.exe" and process.command_line : ("* -enc *", "* -encodedcommand *", "* -ec *", "* -e *")
false_positives: Management agents and installers that pass scripts with -EncodedCommand (for example SCCM or Intune scripts). Allow-list them by signed parent process and host group, not by command line.

name: LSASS memory read access
description: A process opened lsass.exe with PROCESS_VM_READ (0x10) in the granted access mask, which credential dumpers need.
query: any where event.code == "10" and winlog.event_data.TargetImage : "*lsass.exe" and modulo(number(winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess, 16), 32) >= 16
false_positives: Security products (Defender MsMpEng.exe, EDR sensors) and Windows Error Reporting legitimately read LSASS memory. Exclude them by verified executable path and signature.

name: LSASS dump via comsvcs.dll MiniDump
description: rundll32 calling the MiniDump export of comsvcs.dll (by name or ordinal #24) to write a process memory dump.
query: any where event.code in ("1", "4688") and process.command_line : "*comsvcs*" and process.command_line : ("*minidump*", "*#24*")
false_positives: Rare. Troubleshooting sessions may dump processes with comsvcs.dll, but dumping lsass.exe this way should always be investigated.

name: Service installed to run a command interpreter
description: A new service whose binary path launches cmd, PowerShell or another interpreter, as PsExec-style remote execution does.
query: any where (event.code == "7045" and winlog.event_data.ImagePath : ("*%COMSPEC%*", "*cmd*", "*powershell*", "*mshta*", "*rundll32*")) or (event.code == "4697" and winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName : ("*%COMSPEC%*", "*cmd*", "*powershell*", "*mshta*", "*rundll32*"))
false_positives: Software deployment tools and legitimate PsExec use by administrators install short-lived services that run cmd. Correlate with change records.

name: Scheduled task created to run a script interpreter
description: schtasks /create or a new task (4698) whose action runs PowerShell, cmd or a script host.
query: any where (event.code in ("1", "4688") and process.name : "schtasks.exe" and process.command_line : "*/create*" and process.command_line : ("*powershell*", "*cmd*", "*wscript*", "*cscript*", "*mshta*")) or (event.code == "4698" and winlog.event_data.TaskContent : ("*powershell*", "*cmd.exe*", "*wscript*", "*cscript*", "*mshta*"))
false_positives: Administrative and vendor maintenance tasks often run PowerShell. Baseline existing task names per host group and alert on new ones.

name: Script host spawning PowerShell
description: wscript or cscript starting PowerShell, typical of VBScript or JScript droppers.
query: any where event.code in ("1", "4688") and process.parent.name : ("wscript.exe", "cscript.exe") and process.name : "powershell.exe"
false_positives: Legacy logon or inventory scripts in VBScript that call PowerShell. Allow-list them by script path.

name: Kerberos password spraying from one source
description: One source address causes Kerberos failures for at least five different accounts within five minutes: unknown principal (4768, 0x6) or bad password during pre-authentication (4771, 0x18).
query:
FROM threatfusion-windows-otrf
| WHERE (event.code == "4771" AND winlog.event_data.Status == "0x18") OR (event.code == "4768" AND winlog.event_data.Status == "0x6")
| EVAL source_ip = REPLACE(winlog.event_data.IpAddress, "^::ffff:", "")
| STATS failures = COUNT(*), accounts = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source_ip, threatfusion.dataset, window = BUCKET(@timestamp, 5 minutes)
| WHERE accounts >= 5
false_positives: A misconfigured service or a stale mapped drive retrying old credentials across several accounts, and NAT or proxy addresses aggregating many users. Check whether the accounts exist and whether any attempt later succeeded.

name: Kerberoasting: RC4 service ticket for a user service account
description: A domain controller issues a service ticket encrypted with RC4-HMAC (0x17) for a service that is not a computer account or krbtgt. Kerberoasting tools request RC4 because its hash cracks far faster than AES.
query: any where event.code == "4769" and winlog.event_data.Status == "0x0" and winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType == "0x17" and not winlog.event_data.ServiceName : ("*$", "krbtgt")
false_positives: Legacy service accounts whose msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes still allows only RC4, and old clients that cannot do AES. Inventory those SPNs and move them to AES rather than allow-listing the requester.

name: Kerberoasting burst: RC4 tickets for many services from one source
description: One source address receives RC4 service tickets for at least five different non-computer services within five minutes, the request pattern of tools that roast every SPN they enumerate.
query:
FROM threatfusion-windows-otrf
| WHERE event.code == "4769" AND winlog.event_data.Status == "0x0" AND winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType == "0x17" AND NOT winlog.event_data.ServiceName LIKE "*$" AND winlog.event_data.ServiceName != "krbtgt"
| EVAL source_ip = REPLACE(winlog.event_data.IpAddress, "^::ffff:", "")
| STATS requests = COUNT(*), services = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.ServiceName), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source_ip, threatfusion.dataset, window = BUCKET(@timestamp, 5 minutes)
| WHERE services >= 5
false_positives: A legacy application server that opens sessions to many RC4-only services at startup. It repeats on a schedule from a fixed host; an interactive burst from a workstation does not.

name: Failed logon burst: password guessing or spraying from one source
description: At least ten failed logons, or failures for at least five different accounts, from one source within five minutes. The source is the client address, or the workstation name when the logon carries no address (local and NTLM logons).
query:
FROM threatfusion-windows-otrf
| WHERE event.code == "4625"
| EVAL source = CASE(winlog.event_data.IpAddress IS NOT NULL AND winlog.event_data.IpAddress != "-", REPLACE(winlog.event_data.IpAddress, "^::ffff:", ""), winlog.event_data.WorkstationName)
| STATS failures = COUNT(*), accounts = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source, threatfusion.dataset, window = BUCKET(@timestamp, 5 minutes)
| WHERE failures >= 10 OR accounts >= 5
false_positives: A service or scheduled task with a changed password retrying every minute, a user locked out on a mobile device, and shared terminal servers or NAT addresses. Check SubStatus (0xc000006a wrong password, 0xc0000064 unknown user) and whether a success followed.

name: NTLM validation failures for many accounts from one workstation
description: A domain controller rejects NTLM credential validation at least ten times, or for at least five different accounts, from one workstation within five minutes. This is the domain-side view of NTLM guessing and spraying.
query:
FROM threatfusion-windows-otrf
| WHERE event.code == "4776" AND winlog.event_data.Status != "0x0"
| EVAL source = winlog.event_data.Workstation
| STATS failures = COUNT(*), accounts = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source, threatfusion.dataset, window = BUCKET(@timestamp, 5 minutes)
| WHERE failures >= 10 OR accounts >= 5
false_positives: Applications that validate stored credentials for many accounts, and workstation names that are blank or spoofed, since 4776 records the name the client supplies. Pair with 4625 on the target and network logs before blocking a host.
